Devices Dealers Blog About Studios OnomatoPedal Merch EarthQuaker Devices Info Email Search Menu EarthQuaker Devices Info Email Search Devices Dealers Blog About Studios OnomatoPedal Merch Blog Posts Plumes: A Tube Screamer style transparent overdrive pedal, but much more of its own thing than just a TS808 clone. September 17, 2019 Guest User One of the most important features of the Plumes® Small Signal Shredder is that Jamie used it on his own pedalboard for a long time before releasing it for everyone to use. Not to say that he hasn’t done that with other EarthQuaker designs, because he most certainly has. But this is the case of a designer who wasn’t necessarily crazy about a specific circuit, created something that he enjoyed using, and brought the whole thing to another level for everyone else. The use on stage and at band practice is where one can really hear what a pedal is lacking, and which attributes rise to the top. This obsession with testing and refining a circuit into something special is what makes Plumes stand alone in a vast sea of Tube Screamer-style transparent overdrives. The first thing you will notice about Plumes is that it is loud. Loud but not noisy. This is a very “deliberate” sounding pedal. You will hear your pickups and playing. You will get a big result without a lot of knob turning or maxing out the controls. In fact, Plumes is a Tube Screamer-style pedal with a clarity and presence that I have never really experienced before. The components in Plumes were chosen to provide reliability and a more “audio grade” experience overall. Stepping on Plumes is like taking a packing blanket off your speaker. That’s pretty much what it sounds like to me. And if you don’t like things too overdriven, you can still benefit from Plumes’ hi-fi tonality. This is a very cost-effective and simple way to turn a lifeless budget guitar into a sparkle machine. The tone control is pretty much worth the price of admission for me. Turn it clockwise past noon to wake up a boring sounding or low-output guitar. Turn it counterclockwise to tame pickups that you may have deemed too bright in the past. Use it on your bass pedalboard for great grit, with minimal low-end loss. Having the ability to use momentary switching via Flexi-Switch® Technology comes in handy when experimenting with song parts. Plumes is a great way to own a quality piece of gear, that is hand made in the USA by people who love what they do. Mode 1 : Denim Warriors Gibson Les Paul Mode 1 is LED clipping, and by far the raunchiest overdrive. The gain control starts to wake up at about 1 o’clock with colder single coil pickups. Before that, it stays relatively tame. You can hear the full body that is added to your signal, even with gain in the lower settings. This is the mode you will use if you want to get great overdrive but aren’t necessarily using a high-gain amp. If you do use this mode with a high-gain amp with five or more gain stages, you can achieve an almost death metal hotness, with an added dimension and clarity. Let’s not forget the TONE control on Plumes, which never gets muddy, even all the way cut. I find this mode most useful for finely sculpting my overdrive. sources.bodyExcerpt: EarthQuaker Devices Plumes Overdrive Review Guide Skip to content Dirty Guitar Facts. Loud Legends. Specs, tones, and confirmed player guide. admin 22 September 2026 16 min read GG-ARTICLE-TOP Akron, Ohio doesn’t have a coastline or a legendary studio district, but for a certain breed of guitar obsessive, it has something better: EarthQuaker Devices. And the Plumes is the pedal that turned a cult brand into a household name — without selling out a single quirk. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO How to Get the Tone ↓ In the Beginning: A Dead Horse Worth Beating Again By 2019, the world did not need another Tube Screamer derivative. The format had been dissected, cloned, modded, and eulogized roughly ten thousand times over. The JRC4558 op-amp had more tribute acts than the Rolling Stones. So when EarthQuaker Devices founder Jamie Stillman sat down to design a TS-style overdrive for his catalog, he could have coasted. He didn’t. The Plumes Small Signal Shredder was unveiled at Summer NAMM 2019 and hit store shelves on August 3rd of that year. EarthQuaker’s own product copy is typically self-deprecating: “You can’t get enough of it, so we are giving you some more. Doctor’s orders and what not.” The copy sold itself short. Sweetwater named it a hot pick, Premier Guitar handed it a Premier Gear Award, and within months it was one of the fastest-moving EQD products ever. Guitarists who had spent years avoiding yet another screamer were buying it by the handful. The reason? Stillman tore out the canonical guts of the circuit and replaced them with something better. Out went the sacred JRC4558 IC and the bipolar transistor buffers that every other screamer uses. In came JFET operational amplifiers — field-effect transistors in the op-amp stage — and input impedance raised to nearly ten megaohms. On paper that’s an engineering detail. In practice it means less noise, better signal integrity, more chime at the top end, and a low-end response that doesn’t vanish into the circuit the way a classic 4558-based screamer’s can. There’s also a power trick inside the box: the Plumes takes your standard 9-volt supply and internally converts it to plus/minus 9 volts, giving the op-amp a full 18-volt rail to breathe on. That’s the headroom story — and it’s a real one. Where vintage screamer clones can compress and flatten when you dig in hard, the Plumes opens up. EarthQuaker calls it “almost three-dimensional clarity.” That’s marketing language, but this particular marketing language is accurate. Devices Dealers Blog About Studios OnomatoPedal Merch EarthQuaker Devices Info Email Search Menu EarthQuaker Devices Info Email Search Devices Dealers Blog About Studios OnomatoPedal Merch Sound Shank THIS DEVICE IS NO LONGER IN PRODUCTION Sound Shank The Sound Shank is an aggressive germanium fuzz device based on the vintage “Buzzaround” fuzz device. Loads of gain textures on tap through the use of the Sustain control, from subtle grit with loose ends through a tight and focused crunch. The Timbre takes it from paper thin AM radio waves through big, bottom heavy grind and the level shoots it all through your amp with more than enough to spare. This version of the Sound Shank differs from the earlier units. It has been updated for a wider gain range, negative ground for the use of a standard power supply and top mounted jacks. Each Sound Shank is dated and numbered and come with a hand signed certificate of authenticity. Switching-type power supplies, daisy chains and non-pedal specific power supplies do not filter dirty power as well and let through unwanted noise. Do not run at higher voltages! Paul's Boutique Vintage Guitars, Amps and More! Greetings! My name is Paul and I began collecting guitars about seven years ago. I have had a great opportunity to play a plethora of electric guitars from as far back as the 50's I have always had a certain curiosity between certain models of guitar and the associated genre with which they were played. For example, it is because of the stylistic nuances of the jazzmaster that Nels Cline was able to paint such a jovial and melodic picture in the "Impossible Germany" solo, but it was also because of the suspended strings behind the bridge that Thurston Moore was able to conjure such dissonant noisey aggression during his time in Sonic Youth . The Fender Stratocaster? From Hendrix all the way to Holly. Gibson Les Paul? Larry Carlton to Eddie Van Halen. My collection of guitars changes just as rapidly as my taste in music and I am on a quest to find a few trusted allies.
